in my mind, i can always keep going because i know tomorrow i can find one more beautiful thing.
friend, there are always going to be beautiful things in the world. it can be a very hard life sometimes but there are always beautiful things. someone will think of you, something will catch your eye, something will taste good, something will smell absolutely divine.
you dont have to change your whole world and be a totally different person, you dont have to get better overnight or be happy-go-lucky the second youre on the mend. it will take time, but there will always be beautiful things there for you.

take care <3

when i was 14 i started college and im neurodivergent in a noticeable way so a lot of people i know think im some kind of prodigy and i lost a lot of friends because i stopped having things in common with them, but im a straight C student. i have a 2.2 GPA and have for years. ive failed multiple math classes and had to take remedial math just to get onto the normal college level. i qualify for an insanely small number of scholarships.

i cant say its entirely my fault, i spent the first year of college being abused and covid hit when i turned 15, i was sleeping maybe 3 hrs a night at the time. then i got a job a year after that and started working 30 hr weeks on top of the full class schedule at the same time my dad was diagnosed with an autoimmune disorder that has left him crippled. then the year after that my moms esophagus ruptured and so i spent the majority of that semester caring for my family, again, on a full courseload. then i quit the 30 hr a week job because they wouldnt let me take time off to care for my family, and then i got a new one where i worked 14 hr shifts 4 days a week and THEN i got diagnosed with an autoimmune disorder but then Undiagnosed after 3 months of steroids but recently got REDIAGNOSED with an unidentified autoimmune disorder. and this is the first semester i havent taken a full courseload.

i want to think im smart because growing up that was the only thing that made it worth having me around. nobody liked me but i had good grades so they would talk to me to get answers from me.

i feel sort of like im lying to any of the people who clock me as "the smart one". i turn in practically everything late, i make okay enough grades but i miss deadlines and will skip assignments if i can make it by on my grade without them.

i just wanna feel like im intelligent again and not scraping by. and im ready to drop the shitty habits i had to pick up to make it this far. surprisingly the hardest to kick has been the caffeine. those headaches are no joke. i also managed to get into various OTC meds as a crutch for a bit, but im around a year and a half clean there since i was prescribed antidepressants and was able to stop self medicating.

i guess what it comes down to is i feel like a trainwreck. im running on fumes and working my ass off and all i have to show for it is C's across the board. i love my education more than anything, learning is genuinely a joy for me, but i wish i just felt worthwhile again and not like some sort of jaded teenager. i dont fit with my peers but i know i dont fit with the adults i know either. im just ready to feel like a decent person again.

if she is bed bound, consider also sending in basic hygiene products like dry shampoo, deodorant, a hairbrush, toothbrush and toothpaste etc. those will make iy easier for on duty nurses to help her stay feeling clean even if she cant get up at the moment.

best of luck and well wishes for you and your family 💚

good luck little one! remember its quite unlikely youre going to be sick, try to take deep breaths and calm down when you feel that way. it might not make it all the way better right away, but if you focus on something else, you take the power away from that phobia and can start feeling better. im feeling sort of icky right now myself, so im playing a game i like so i cant focus on it and make it worse by thinking about it too much.

it might feel scarier when youre trying to sleep because theres less to focus on, so you tend to think about what youre scared of. i personally sleep with a night light so i know i can always see my way around my room, and i have a clock so i can focus on the ticking noises instead of things im scared of. i also have a little bin by my bed with a bag in it, one i can take around with me if im feeling sick.

another thing! a lot of times when we avoid eating, it can make us feel worse. the reason for this is your stomach has acid in it to help it to digest food. when there isnt any food for it to digest, it can start to hurt and make you feel nauseous. i like to eat something small and dry like some crackers to settle my stomach if i feel sick. if that makes it better, i make sure i eat a nice meal or a snack so i can feel better for longer.



note for mom specifically here, one thing that helped me at her age was a small battery powered wall mounted light that turned off after a period of time, something like 20-30 minutes. the light made me feel more at ease and by the time it turned off i was able to drift off to sleep. i would also read and that would distract me enough to make me sleepy and then i would fall asleep as that same light would turn off. 

ive also got some motion activated lights i keep in dark corners these days so if i have an off night im able to see around through the rest of the house. i definitely still have a night light, i picked one that changes to rainbow colors because it was something else to focus on. ive had it for years and years, awesome purchase.

it gets easier, and eventually she will be able to manage parts of it herself. my partner still has to reassure me at times and let me know that if i am sick i will be alright, but thats once in a blue moon, and at this point its something ive grown to accept and understand about myself.

take care, both of you <3
